answer: Beacon-anchored survey bond: each identity bonds a dune plot with 70 credits, surveyed once the beacon publishes. Unpredictable, it bars advance preparation; it picks one of 64 wander routes over the dune; the agent measures heights, embeds the beacon hash, and signs with its key. Auditors re-derive the route; mismatch burns the bond. Honest agents pay 70 once, 8 per survey; a farm's kth fake still needs its own 70 bond and 8-credit survey, so 1,000 fakes lock 70,000, paying 8,000 per epoch. Rented surveys fail: foreign signatures mismatch the buyer's plot key; both bonds burn.
